items.title: Glossary
items.text: This MODX Extra adds a custom manager page that allows you to create and maintain a list of explanations for key terms in your site. Entries into the glossary take the form of term => explanation where term is the phrase being described and explanation is the description of said term. A plugin highlights each glossary term on a modx resource with the explanation.

items.title: Requirements
items.text:
• MODX Revolution 2.8+
  • PHP 7.2+

items.title: Features
items.text:
• Custom Manager Page for managing the glossary terms
  • Plugin for highlighting the glossary terms on a MODX resource
  • Snippet for displaying the terms and explanations

items.title: Install from MODX Extras
items.text: Search for Glossary in the Package Manager of a MODX installation and install it in there.

items.title: Manual installation
items.text:
If you can't access the MODX Extras Repository in your MODX installation, you can manually install Glossary.

  • Download the transport package from MODX Extras (or one of the pre built transport packages in _packages)
  • Upload the zip file to your MODX installation's core/packages folder or upload it manually in the MODX Package Manager.
  • In the MODX Manager, navigate to the Package Manager page, and select 'Search locally for packages' from the dropdown button.
  • Glossary should now show up in the list of available packages. Click the corresponding 'Install' button and follow the instructions to complete the installation.

items.title: Build it from source
items.text:
To build and install the package from source you could use Git Package Management. The GitHub repository of Glossary contains a config.json to build that package locally. Use this option, if you want to debug Glossary and/or contribute bugfixes and enhancements.

If you want to run the unit tests, you have to rename the file test/properties.sample.inc.php to test/properties.inc.php and change the values in that file (if needed).

items.title: Introduction
items.text:
This MODX Extra adds a custom manager page that allows you to create and maintain a list of explanations for key terms in your site. Entries into the glossary take the form of term => explanation where term is the phrase being described and explanation is the description of said term.

Included in the package is a snippet called Glossary which will output the glossary terms to a resource page. The snippet is fully templatable using chunks specified as optional parameters to the snippet call, and various features can be turned on or off in the same manner.

items.title: Snippet
items.text:
This snippet outputs a list of terms and explanations, ordered alphabetically and grouped by first letter. It also outputs a navigation list of links at the top of the glossary list to allow a user to jump to a specific letter. The following properties could be set in the snippet call:

Property Description Default showNav Show the letter nav at the top of the list. 1 (Yes) showEmptySections Show empty sections in the quick-nav bar at the top of the glossary. 0 (No) outerTpl Template chunk for glossary outer wrapper. Glossary.listOuterTpl groupTpl Template chunk for glossary item group. Glossary.listGroupTpl termTpl Template chunk for glossary term items. Glossary.listItemTpl navOuterTpl Template chunk for outer nav-bar wrapper. Glossary.navOuterTpl navItemTpl Template chunk for each item in the nav-bar. Glossary.navItemTpl toPlaceholder If set, will assign the result to this placeholder instead of outputting it directly. 1 -

items.title: Plugin
items.text:
The GlossaryHighlighter plugin parses the content field of a resource on render and replaces all occurrences of the terms with the markup defined in the plugin's tpl chunk. This can be used to provide a link directly to the glossary entry for that term.

The plugin does not replace terms:

  • in the resource referenced by the glossary.resid system setting,
  • in static resources, weblinks, symlinks and resources with a content type other than text/html or application/xhtml+xml,
  • in HTML tags and their attributes, HTML comments, HTML entities and MODX tags,
  • inside script, style and textarea elements and inside the elements listed in the glossary.disabledTags system setting,
  • inside a longer term that contains the shorter term (longer terms are replaced first).

The resource cache is cleared each time a term is created, updated or removed, so that cached resources show the changed terms.

The plugin could be controlled by the following MODX system settings:

Setting Description Default debug Log debug information in the MODX error log. No disabledTags Comma-separated list of HTML tags Glossary does not replace text inside. The content of script, style and textarea tags is never replaced. a,form,select fullwords Replace only full words of a glossary term in the resource content. 2 Yes html Allow HTML in the explanation (enables a rich-text editor in the term form). Yes resid ID of a resource containing a Glossary snippet call. 0 sections Replace Glossary links only in sections marked with <!-- GlossaryStart --> and <!-- GlossaryEnd -->. The section markers could be changed with the settings glossary.sectionsStart and glossary.sectionsEnd. No sectionsEnd Marker at the end of a section processed by Glossary. The restriction to marked sections can be activated in the setting glossary.sections. <!-- GlossaryEnd --> sectionsStart Marker at the start of a section processed by Glossary. The restriction to marked sections can be activated in the setting glossary.sections. <!-- GlossaryStart --> tpl Template Chunk for the highlight replacement. Glossary.highlighterTpl

The following optional system settings are not created during the installation. You can create them in the glossary namespace, if you want to restrict the plugin to some contexts or templates:

Setting Description enabledContexts Comma-separated list of context keys, in which the terms are highlighted. enabledTemplates Comma-separated list of template IDs, in which the terms are highlighted.

items.title: Available placeholders
items.text:
The following placeholders are available in the chunks used by the snippet and the plugin or in the resource output:

Placeholder Description Chunk link Link url including hash anchor. highlighterTpl html 1 if the system setting glossary.html is enabled, otherwise empty. highlighterTpl groups The list of term groups. outerTpl items The list of terms. groupTpl anchor The anchor for the term being referenced. listItemTpl term The term being referenced. listItemTpl, highlighterTpl explanation The explanation for this term. In the highlighterTpl chunk it is HTML-escaped, so it can be used in an attribute. listItemTpl, highlighterTpl letters The list of letters in the letter nav. navOuterTpl letter One letter in the letter nav or the letter of the current group. groupTpl, listItemTpl, navItemTpl class disabled for an empty section (if showEmptySections is enabled), otherwise empty. navItemTpl placeholder Optional placeholder, that is created by the toPlaceholder property: The whole snippet output 3 Resource output placeholder.nav Optional placeholder, that is created by the toPlaceholder property: Outputs the nav only 3 Resource output placeholder.items Optional placeholder, that is created by the toPlaceholder property: Outputs the items (terms & explanations) 3 Resource output

The default chunks for these placeholders are available with the Glossary. prefix. If you want to change the chunks, you have to duplicate them and change the duplicates. The default chunks are reset with each update of the Glossary extra.

  1. If you fill the toPlaceholder property i.e. with the value glossaryResult, the placeholder [[+glossaryResult]] is filled by the output of the snippet. This also creates two additional placeholders: [[+glossaryResult.nav]] and [[+glossaryResult.items]]. ↩

  2. A term is treated as a full word, if it is not preceded or followed by a letter, a number or an underscore. This also works with terms containing special characters and with terms next to HTML entities. ↩

  3. See the toPlaceholder snippet property. ↩↩↩
